by: second master sommelier, the facts read after the researchers and the refuters

searches.note: Each search is counted on the check it served; four checks took more than one (Thanisch three; Williams Selyem, Dr. Loosen and Huet two each), for a second question or where a first search drifted (Thanisch to another branch of the family, Faiveley to a railway, Huet's camp to other camps) and was run again more narrowly. Every check that confirmed a fact rests on two independent sources or on one primary; none went unsourced, so nothing was removed for want of a search.

method: Every one of the 255 records was read in full for its facts (place, founding year, the wine's appellation, rank, grapes, sites, making, ageing, label, table line, story, others and traps), group by group against the review files, then across groups: every person named with dates was gathered into one list and each pair of dates compared and checked against what is known; serving temperatures were tabulated by colour against the Codex's service reference; founding years were read against the library; repeated facts (the appellation and decree years, the Paris tasting, the Swartland Revolution, the Jordan division of 1848, the DAC years) were compared record against record and against the Codex's own data files.

Spot checks went to the strongest claims first: the deaths and dates of people of the last few years (a living person named as dead would break two rules at once), recent ownership changes, claims of a first or an only, classification and decree years, the facts a refuter had left open, and then the dated milestones a guest is likeliest to ask about.
A search summary drawn from a body's or a house's own domain is read as that body; the sources of every check are listed with it. No WebFetch was tried.

Fragments were changed only where a check showed a fact wrong, unsettled or volatile, or a serving temperature out of line; each change was linted sound with build-flagships.cjs --lint, and the writing build was never run. plan.json, people.json and the Codex's own files were not edited: what they need is listed under planWhys and codex.

fixes.was: 8 to 10 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle briefly so the struck match can clear; a white wine glass.
fixes.now: 6 to 8 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle briefly so the struck match can clear; a white wine glass.
fixes.why: an Auslese is a sweet white: the Codex's service reference and the WSET give 6 to 8, and every other sweet white of the roster stands there

fixes.was: 8 to 10 degrees Celsius; no need to decant; a white wine glass and a modest pour, with blue cheese or a fruit tart.

crossChecks: Founding years: 206 records carry a producerId, and each record's founded was read against the library's founded for that house. They agree but for three where the record is empty and the library gives a century or a round year (Armand Rousseau, Bruno Giacosa, Biondi-Santi), one where the library gives a sentence for its year (Weinbach, 1898 in both), and eleven where the library has none; an empty field is a true answer, so none is changed.

Serving temperatures were tabulated by colour against the Codex's service reference: every wine falls in its band but those that name whose advice they follow (Coulée de Serrant's 13 to 15, the estate's; the warmer Madeiras, the island's or the house's; Harveys and Fefiñanes, the house's), and the two Mosel Auslesen, the only sweet whites out of line, which are fixed.

Decree and classification years told in more than one record or against the Codex were compared: Taurasi DOC 1970 and DOCG 1993, Bolgheri Sassicaia a sub-zone from 1994 and a DOC of its own from 2013, Valpolicella Ripasso a DOC from 2010, Conegliano Valdobbiadene DOC 1969 and DOCG 2009, Barbaresco DOC 1966 and DOCG 1980, the Gran Vinya Classificada from 2017, the Wachau DAC's Ried from 2020, Grange Hermitage up to the 1989 vintage, and Romanée-Conti's replanting; record and record, and record and Codex, agree on each.

Living persons: every name in the 255 records was read; the only living names are in the names of houses, wines or vineyards (Mark Bradford, Julia Lee's Block, Kevin John, Peter Barlow) and architects' firms, which the house rules allow. No price, score or allocation was found; superlatives of judgement were already caught by the lint.
